svg.title: Interactions, work & springs
svg.desc: Contact or non-contact: Contact: friction, drag, tension, normal force. Non-contact: gravity, electrostatic, magnetic. Scalar: speed, mass, energy. Vector: force, velocity, momentum. Arrow length and direction represent a vector. Weight & components: W = mg, N = kg × N/kg; weight acts at centre of mass. Mass stays the same if g changes. For angled forces, draw tip-to-tail at a stated scale. Diagonal = resultant; perpendicular components have the same combined effect. Work done: W = Fs, distance along force. 40 N × 3 m = 120 J. Work against friction warms surfaces. A stationary object needs more than one force to change shape: pulls at opposite ends, for example. Hooke’s law: F = ke up to proportional limit. 6 N / 0.030 m = 200 N/m. Elastic = recovers shape; inelastic = permanent. Losing proportionality need not immediately mean permanent deformation. Spring practical: Record unloaded length; add known loads; let settle; read length at eye level. Extension = loaded − original. F = mg includes hanger. Repeat; secure stand, avoid overload and falling masses. Graph & stored energy: F vertical vs e horizontal: straight-line gradient = k. Unload to test elastic recovery. Eₑ = ½ke², triangular area under proportional F–e graph. Do not use final force × extension.
